parole.testo: Borrowed from taxonomic name Brachiosaurus, itself a learned borrowing from Ancient Greek βραχίων (brakhíōn) + σαῦρος (saûros).

parole.significato: any vesper bat of the genus Nyctophilus (long-eared bat)
parole.testo: Calque of taxonomic name Nyctophilus, from noc (“night”) + -o- + lubić (“to like, to enjoy”) + -ek.

parole.significato: petunia (any plant of the genus Petunia)
parole.testo: (This etymology is missing or incomplete. Please add to it, or discuss it at the Etymology scriptorium. Particularly: “etydate: WSJP says "1900, NKJP", but no such concordance in PELCRA”) Learned borrowing from taxonomic name Petunia, from (now obsolete) French pétun (“tobacco”), from Old Tupi petym
